BEGIN_PGML Line [`A`] and Line [`B`] are perpendicular. Line [`A`]'s equation is [`2x+3y=12\text{.}`] Line [`B`] passes through the point [`(4,-3)\text{.}`] Find an equation for Line [`B\text{.}`]
[_]{$line}{20}
END_PGML
########## # Solution ##########
BEGIN_PGML_SOLUTION First, we will find Line [`A`]'s slope by rewriting its equation from standard form to slope-intercept form:
[``` \begin{aligned} 2x+3y\amp=12\\ 3y\amp=12\subtractright{2x}\\ 3y\amp=-2x+12\\ y\amp=\divideunder{-2x+12}{3}\\ y\amp=-\frac{2}{3}x+4 \end{aligned} ```]
So Line [`A`]'s slope is [`-\frac{2}{3}\text{.}`] Since Line [`B`] is perpendicular to Line [`A\text{,}`] its slope is the negative reciprocal, [`\frac{3}{2}\text{.}`] It's also given that Line [`B`] passes through [`(4,-3)\text{,}`] so we can write Line [`B`]'s point-slope form equation:
[``` \begin{aligned} y\amp=m(x-x_0)+y_0\\ y\amp=\frac{3}{2}(x-4)-3 \end{aligned} ```]
END_PGML_SOLUTION
